question: Should OpenClaw adopt the public plugin readiness callback and the four built-in hosting profiles as supported configuration and readiness contracts in this release line?
rationale: The branch adds a compatibility-sensitive Plugin SDK API plus new config, environment, CLI, protocol, and readiness behavior; code review cannot determine the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Approve the V1 readiness contract
options.body: Confirm the public Plugin SDK and profile-selection contract, then require exact-head package-installed Docker proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to core-only profiles
options.body: Keep hosting-profile work internal to core-owned observations and defer the public plugin readiness callback until a separate SDK decision.

options.title: Defer the feature stack
options.body: Pause the readiness/profile rollout until maintainers want to own its compatibility and release-test burden.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 readiness contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the public Plugin SDK and profile-selection contract, then require exact-head package-installed Docker proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate for a cross-cutting core and Plugin SDK product-contract decision.
